newsitem.title: GERMANY: U.S. says Zaire troop meeting now set for Thursday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says Zaire troop meeting now set for Thursday.

text.p: The U.S. military said on Monday a meeting in Germany of countries participating in a Canadian-led force to help refugees in Zaire had been rescheduled to Thursday, a day later than originally planned.

"I have been told that the meeting will be on Thursday," U.S. Navy Captain Timothy Taylor, director of public affairs for the U.S. European Command in Stuttgart, told Reuters. The European command will host the meeting to be led by Canada.
Taylor said the Canadians who will lead the meeting are scheduled to arrive in Stuttgart on Tuesday and Wednesday.
He did not know why the meeting date had been changed from Wednesday, as announced on Sunday at the World Food Summit in Rome by South African Deputy President Thabo Mbeki.

The meeting has been called to discuss the scope of the mission now that half a million Rwandan refugees have returned home, raising doubts among some members of the proposed peace force about the need for military intervention.
Britain, France and Spain said earlier on Monday they expected the mission to go ahead with a redefined plan to open up humanitarian corridors to aid refugees.

The United States said on Sunday it would decide in the next few days if it needed to send troops to Zaire, prompting reports that the U.S. and other nations were having second thoughts about the need for intervention in Zaire.
U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry said on Sunday Washington had yet to make a firm decision on participation.
"We are not the Salvation Army," he said in a television interview.
The United Nations refugee agency UNHCR said on Monday half a million Hutu refugees had now crossed back into Rwanda from Zaire and more were on the way.
The refugees, Hutus who fled the arrival in power of a Tutsi-led movement in 1994, began returing last week after Zairean rebels forced Hutu fighters to flee to the hills.
